newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says will counter Cyprus EU bid. [CORRECTED 11:33 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Turkey says will counter Cyprus EU bid. [CORRECTED 11:33 GMT]

text.p: Deputy Prime Minister Bulent (Corrects) Ecevit said on Wednesday that Turkey would respond sharply if plans to bring Cyprus into the European Union weakened the position of Turkish Cypriots.
"Any step taken in connection with Cyprus which we or Turkish Cyprus do not accept will be more than met by our own steps," Ecevit told a meeting of his leftist party's MPs.
He warned on Tuesday that the Turkish Cypriot north of the divided island would be integrated into Turkey if the EU went ahead with membership talks with the Cypriot government as planned next year.

The government, run by Greek Cypriots and recognised internationally as the only administration on the island, on Wednesday hailed a European Commission commitment to include it in EU expansion talks and said the move could help resolve the Cyprus problem.
Ankara says allowing Cyprus to join before solving the division of the Mediterranean island would only reinforce the tensions between Greek and Turkish Cypriots.

Cyprus has been divided since 1974 when Turkey invaded the northern third of the island in response to a short-lived coup in Nicosia backed by the military junta then ruling Greece. A Turkish Cypriot state in the north is recognised only by Ankara.
Ecevit, a veteran leftist who returned to power last month in a right-left coalition, was prime minister in 1974 and gave the order to invade.
On Tuesday Europe reaffirmed its commitment to open accession talks with Cyprus, along with the Czech Republic, Poland, Hungary, Slovenia and Estonia, next year.
